versions.short: The bill would authorize an Environmental Protection Agency initiative to find and recover critical materials, such as minerals that are at high risk of supply disruption and are essential to energy technologies, from contaminated sites. The agency would investigate and support methods for identifying where these materials are and recovering them, and it could give assistance such as awards to individuals, nonprofit groups, and state, local, and tribal governments. The bill would cap total assistance at $10 million in any fiscal year and limit any single recipient to $3 million. The program would end after 10 years.
